**Resh (ר)** is the `20th letter of the Hebrew alphabet`.[[1]](https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/137092/jewish/Resh.htm)

### Key Facts

- **Sound:** Pronounced like an "R" (typically a uvular or throat-based "R" in modern Hebrew, similar to French or German, or an alveolar "R").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resh)[[2]](https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/137092/jewish/Resh.htm)[[3]](https://kriakala.com/hebrew-letter-resh)
- **Numerical Value:** 200 in Gematria (Jewish system of assigning numbers to letters).[[1]](https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/137092/jewish/Resh.htm)
- **Meaning:** Derived from the Hebrew word *rosh* (רֹאשׁ), meaning **"head,"** **"chief,"** or **"beginning"**.[[1]](https://learnhebrewforchristians.com/hebrew-alphabet/resh)[[2]](https://kriakala.com/hebrew-letter-resh)
- **Visual Shape:** Composed of one vertical line and one curved horizontal line forming a profile of a head or a bowed figure. It looks similar to the letter *Dalet* (ד), except *Dalet* has a sharp corner (a *yud* ) at the top right, while *Resh* is rounded.[[1]](https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/137092/jewish/Resh.htm)[[2]](https://kriakala.com/hebrew-letter-resh)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ybH-yeU-rIc)

### Symbolism & Significance

- **Leadership and Mind:** Because it means "head," *Resh* represents the mind, intellect, and leadership—signifying that actions and new beginnings originate in the thoughts.[[1]](https://learnhebrewforchristians.com/hebrew-alphabet/resh)
- **Common Examples:** It appears in words like *Rosh Hashanah* (Head of the Year / Jewish New Year), *Beresheet* (In the beginning, from Genesis 1:1), and *Ruach* (spirit or wind).[[1]](https://gabrielelevy.com/pages/the-letter-resh)[[2]](https://learnhebrewforchristians.com/hebrew-alphabet/resh)[[3]](https://kriakala.com/hebrew-letter-resh)[[4]](https://invasionoflight.com/2021/11/01/resh-our-head-shepherd-revealer-of-truth/)[[5]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ybH-yeU-rIc)[[6]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qmisfotK92g&t=430)
- **Duality:** In Jewish tradition, *Resh* can symbolize a person who is a *rosh* (a head/leader) or, at its lower extreme, a *rasha* (a wicked or spiritually poor person), carrying a choice between wisdom and corruption.[[1]](https://hebrewtoday.com/alphabet/the-letter-resh-%D7%A8/)[[2]](https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/137092/jewish/Resh.htm)

You can read more about its deeper meanings on [Chabad.org](https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/137092/jewish/Resh.htm) or check its historical evolution on [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resh).[[1]](https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/137092/jewish/Resh.htm)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resh)Would you like to explore how *Resh* compares to *Dalet* , or look at other letters in the Hebrew alphabet?
